item.title: John Constantine Movie From Evil Dead Wrath Filmmaker is in Development at DC
item.description:
DC Studios has tapped Evil Dead Wrath writer-director Francis Galluppi to pen a John Constantine movie for the studio.
The news comes via Deadline in a report that suggests the project is still very early on in development. It's not known if Galluppi will be handling directorial duties in addition to his work on the script, and there's been no mention of any casting details at this time.
John Constantine is a comic book character created by writer Alan Moore and artists Steve Bissette and John Totleben, and is a working-class British detective who dabbles in the occult and magic.
Keanu Reeves famously played a version of the character in 2005's Constantine, and a sequel has been anticipated by fans for quite a number of years now. In late 2025, Reeves issued an update on Constantine 2, telling Fandango that a new draft of the sequel's script had been completed and that it was going to be presented to DC Studios. However, there have been no updates since then, and it's not known whether Galluppi's new script is intended to serve as a sequel to Reeves' original, or if it will be a completely new take on the demon-dispatching detective.
Constantine: City of Demons Images
Meanwhile, Galluppi's Evil Dead Wrath is currently scheduled for a theatrical release on April 7, 2028. It will be the seventh installment in the Evil Dead film series, and will serve as a prequel to 1981's The Evil Dead, with its story taking place in 1972. Galluppi developed and brought the story to franchise creator Sam Raimi and his team back in 2024, off the back of the up-and-coming American filmmaker earning critical acclaim for his debut feature, The Last Stop in Yuma County.
Around that time Raimi told Deadline that, "Francis Galluppi is a storyteller who knows when to keep us waiting in simmering tension and when to hit us with explosive violence. He is a director that shows uncommon control in his feature debut."
Tristan Ogilvie is a senior video editor at IGN based in Sydney, Australia. He has 25 years of experience covering video games, having served as Deputy Editor on Official PlayStation 2 Magazine Australia and as Editor of Official Xbox 360 Magazine Australia, before joining IGN in 2009. You can find him on Bluesky @tristanogilvie.bsky.social

item.title: Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job.
item.description:
Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job.
When speaking with Dan Allen Gaming, Sloane was asked if he's interested in reprising his role as Price in the upcoming live-action Call of Duty film. The movie, directed by Peter Berg and written by Taylor Sheridan, is expected to be set in the Modern Warfare universe, but it's unclear if it's a new story or a direct adaptation of one of the games. With that said, it's hard to imagine a Modern Warfare movie without Price. Sloane wants in on the film and even went as far as to say he's the most qualified person on the planet to do it.
"I don't think there's anyone else on the planet who is as qualified for the job as I am," said Sloane. "Who has lived the character for almost a decade? Who understands the size of the projects, the love of that fan base, and has been on the journey with them from the get-go? Hollywood is a beast. Sometimes things are decided for certain reasons that can never be understood. But if you're asking me, would I like to do it? Absolutely, I would love to play him in a movie. 100%. That would be fantastic. But let's let the Hollywood cards fall where they land."
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Screenshots
Sloane also noted that there's been a vocal outpouring from fans to have him play Price in the film, which he massively appreciates. He noted that typically, there's a group of names that a studio wants for a role like this, and they have to go through that process themselves. Nevertheless, he believes he'd be an "asset" to the production if he were to have the opportunity.
As games have gotten increasingly realistic, they've also started to use the likenesses of the actors who play them. This has led to demand from fans that film adaptations should use the actors from the games. Of course, Hollywood might make the argument that they're not as big of a box office draw compared to a more traditional mainstream movie star. Whether Call of Duty will utilize the game's cast remains to be seen.
Spoilers for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 follow below.
Of course, if the Call of Duty movie is canonical to the games, where it falls in the timeline will dictate what characters can show up. Modern Warfare 4 brutally takes a number of characters off the board, including Captain Price. At the end of the game, the character is left to bleed out in the middle of the wilderness, with Ghost having said his goodbyes to his fallen leader. It's a tragic ending for the character, but one that felt right and leaves the future of the Modern Warfare games in question.
With that said, if the Call of Duty movie takes place within the canon, it would have to be set before Modern Warfare 4. If it's a sequel of sorts, it may focus on all-new characters or the surviving ones like Ghost and the Korean characters introduced in MW4. The film is due out in 2028, so we'll likely hear more on casting sometime next year as filming nears.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever launch day live blog.
item.description:
World of Warcraft Forever is finally here, and the gates to this alternate version of Azeroth open at 3 PM PST / 6 PM EST. All the signs from the beta are pointing to Forever being one of the biggest launches in Warcraft history, with so many people testing the game that developers claimed it put up "the craziest numbers" they've seen in 17 years.
Even after expanding the level cap in the beta, it was still capped at level 30, and most people – outside of some promotions – had to buy an expensive Skyborne pack to get in. Once the live servers go up, the only barrier to playing WoW Forever is going to be an active WoW subscription or a friend code. (And there are going to be a lot of friend codes out there.)
But while WoW Forever promises to be a huge launch and a return to form for many WoW fans, the real test is going to be how well the servers hold up. I've been playing Blizzard's games my entire life, and it's pretty much a given that something is going to go wrong when Blizzard flicks the switch to open up the game. Even last week, when Blizzard opened its name reservation system, European players couldn't get in for hours, and American players were greeted with long server queues and disconnects. So, I expect the full launch to be, well, spicy.
World of Warcraft: Forever Screenshots
But I'm going to be in the trenches, trying to get in myself and keeping an eye on the community to find all the cool stuff people are talking about, and gathering all of that here. So, whether you're stuck at work while the servers go up, or you're inevitably frustrated by the servers buckling under the weight of millions of MMO fans, stay tuned for all the fun. Live updates are below.
World of Warcraft Forever Live Blog
All times are in EST
12:45am: After such a successful launch, Blizzard posted about the servers that WoW Forever is running on. And, well, hopefully Sam Altman isn't watching, because apparently the WoWF servers are running on 251,136GB of RAM.
*Slaps Roof of WoW: Forever*This baby is running on:3,924 Virtual Machines251,136 GB of Memory70,480 CPU Cores https://t.co/P9PdRBzke7
8:15 pm: Even a couple hours in, it seems like World of Warcraft Forever is the smoothest Blizzard launch in years. Even after the pain that the servers felt when name reservations went live last week, everything seems pretty buttoned up. I'm seeing fewer and fewer people having problems getting into the game, and the issues now seem limited to folks getting frustrated at faction limits and the sheer amount of people competing for mobs.
I'm going to keep my eyes open for anything else going on, but for most people, you should be able to just log in and get lost in Azeroth. And, that's honestly the highest praise I could give to a massive live game launch like this.
7:43 pm: I'm finally on the way to Brill, and as soon as I got past the gate, I rounded a corner, and got blown away by some incredible lighting. Blizzard really did knock the graphics upgrades out of the park with WoW Forever. If you have powerful enough hardware, trust me, max the game out, at least for a little bit.
7:37 pm: Some more problems are starting to appear. In the forums, there's a thread suggesting that there are AMD driver problems that are causing driver timeouts. Let me know down below if you've been running into driver issues.
Apparently the problem is a black screen, followed by a hard system reboot. And it looks like this bug has persisted through the beta, according to the player who posted the thread. But this might be a problem on AMD's end, rather than Blizzard. The game is running without issue for me on an Nvidia card.
7:22 pm: There are still people stuck at the ruleset menu, and Blizzard hasn't provided an update on that bug yet. But at least people seem to have a sense of humor about it.
7:08 pm: Blizzard is aware of problems with payment processing, so if you're struggling with actually subscribing to the game to play, they're working on it.
@RAM2191 As soon as possible! Website issues are due to the amount of traffic, keep trying as you can, maybe even wait just a few minutes. ^CC
7:00 pm: We're an hour into the launch and the servers feel great. No real lag, and I haven't been disconnected yet. I've also seen some reports of new Horde characters being disabled due to the high demand on PvP servers. So much for people not wanting to play monsters.
Just speaking anecdotally, but there were so many Undead players that I had to group up with four other people to finish one of the first quests. But, that's exactly what Forever's devs want you to do.
6:36 pm: Just killed enough zombies to finish the first quest, there are just so many people in Tirisfal right now. But, while the launch seems to have gone smoothly for most people, I've started seeing some players that are having trouble getting online. Some people are also reporting that the characters they reserved aren't there anymore.
6:30 pm: IGN's review in progress from Len Hafer just went live! There's obviously no verdict yet, but it seems good so far.
6:23 pm: If you're still getting gray rulesets bug, it seems like most people have been able to fix it by closing the game and re-entering the queue. I know it sucks to have to sit in line again, but it seems like the queues are going pretty quick so far. But, of course, that could change.
6:13 pm: Wait, I'm in! Looks like the server is at least working for me, and there's a veritable army of Undead here in Tirisfal Glades. Even in the forums, people seem pleasantly surprised by how quick the server queue went. But there are still some people who are getting kicked offline as soon as they get to the character select screen.
6:10 pm: Blizzard is aware of the problem with 'Rulesets' not being available, and BlizzardCS has reported it to the devs. Hopefully it's a quick fix. But even though it seems like people are going to have to wait a while to get in, it is kind of nostalgic to sit here waiting for the server queue. And I don't seem to be the only one who thinks so.
Is it wrong that I kinda like launches like this https://t.co/Ibjayw6N25
6:05 pm: I'm back in the queue, but this time with 2,135 people ahead of me. I just went to the forums to check if other people are having problems, and the forums are down. Let me know down below if you're able to get in.
6:00 pm: And here we go, World of Warcraft Forever is live, and I was immediately greeted by a login queue. But only with 128 people ahead of me. Not bad! Lets see if I get in. Well, I got in, but all the rulesets are 'temporarily unavailable.' Cool.
5:50 pm: Servers are up in 10 minutes, or at least they're supposed to be. But with the level of excitement that people have for WoWF, I wouldn't be surprised if the servers struggle for a little bit. But no matter what happens, remember, you will get in eventually.
IF YOURE IN LINE AT THE WOW FOREVER LOG IN SCREEN STAY IN LINE DONT LEAVE THEY LEGALLY HAVE TO LET YOU IN THE SERVERS PER THE CONSTITUTION KNOW YOUR RIGHTS 🇺🇸 🇺🇸
5:36 pm: The first legendary weapon in World of Warcraft Forever is a healing weapon called Taldramir, The Whispering Wood. It's cool enough that Blizzard is showing love to healers, but apparently it also had it made in real life, too. I'm getting ready for the launch by logging into retail just one more time before Forever kicks off in earnest.
And, of course, the first thing I see is someone in trade chat saying "alright kids see you in a couple months or years depending on how good Forever is"
A legendary stream deserves a new Legendary Weapon 💥Introducing Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, forged in partnership with @WetaWorkshop 🔨 https://t.co/D3orhPhcM0
5:15 pm: We're 45 minutes out, but people already seem excited to get in.
Today I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. Tomorrow I am playing World of Warcraft forever. The next day I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. The day after that I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. The day after that I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. Forever.
Congratulations to the entire @Warcraft team and best of luck on a great WoW Forever launch!Also wishing a speedy recovery to everyone who suddenly came down with the flu this morning 😔👀
5:00 pm: The servers are scheduled to go online in about an hour, and just in the last couple of days there's been a lot happening for WoW Forever. For instance, in response to the patch notes that went out Monday night, the Shaman class discord shut down in protest of the changes, something that happened with ret Paladins last year in Midnight.
Still, the biggest question on my mind ahead of the launch is 'how will the servers handle the load?' Even in the best case scenario, I expect some pretty beefy server queues that we'll have to sit through. And, as a reminder, there are new Nvidia graphics drivers, so if you're on a Team Green card, take this hour before launch to update your drivers.
World of Warcraft Forever or Retail?

item.title: While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack."
item.description:
While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack.”
The Black Widow star was interviewed by Entertainment Tonight about her new movie Paper Tiger, where she was asked which of her roles in upcoming franchise films (Exorcist: Martyrs or The Batman: Part II) pushed her the most outside of her comfort zone,
“Probably the role in The Batman, because it gave me a lot of existential angst, for some reason,” Johansson explained.
“It was very hard to figure out. I don’t know why, whether it was just the role or it was just where I am in my life, but it was just hard to crack it. And that’s all I can say about it.”
The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel
The rumor mill has suggested Johansson is playing Gilda Dent or Poison Ivy in the sequel.
Johansson isn’t the only cast member who’s been asked about The Batman: Part II in recent interviews. Robert Pattinson has praised the sequel for having "an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology" that he doesn't "think has been seen before."
The Batman: Part II has resumed filming in the UK under the supervision of Steven Soderbergh, who is overseeing the final stages of shooting while director Matt Reeves deals with a family matter. Reeves will resume the directing reins once the film reaches post-production.
Despite the production delays, The Batman: Part II remains scheduled to open in theaters on February 18, 2028.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix were both offered the role of Joker in The Dark Knight, but ended up turning it down, according to the film's casting director.
item.description:
Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix were both offered the role of Joker in The Dark Knight, but ended up turning it down, according to the film's casting director.
When speaking at the Nashville Film Festival (via TV Intelligentsia and Batman News), Christopher Nolan's longtime casting director John Papsidera revealed that Heath Ledger was not the first choice for Joker in The Dark Knight. He said the script was sent to Leonardo DiCaprio first, who apparently didn't even respond. Then, the offer went to Joaquin Phoenix, who would later win an Oscar for the same role in 2019's Joker. Phoenix told Nolan and Papsidera at the time that he wasn't interested in doing big movies and declined the part.
Eventually, they landed on Heath Ledger, and the rest is history. Leonardo DiCaprio went on to star in Nolan's next project, Inception. The actor also stated last year that The Dark Knight was his favorite Nolan film. Warner Bros. reportedly pressured Nolan and his creative team to cast the Titanic star as The Riddler in the third Batman movie. The team went against this idea, since they typically developed the story for Batman first and then tried to figure out a villain. As a result, Bane made for a more logical villain in a story about an aging Batman who is physically outmatched.
And as already noted, Phoenix went on to play a completely different version of the Joker. In his two films, Joker is far less calculated. He's more of a guy who stumbles into becoming a symbol for chaos, revolution, and anarchy, though is wildly out of his depth.
While it may be difficult to imagine DiCaprio as Joker, it's worth reflecting on who Heath Ledger was before he was cast in the role. He was considered a pretty boy in Hollywood, not unlike DiCaprio, and it was seen as an odd choice to cast the actor for such a villainous role. Phoenix wasn't too far beyond that class of actor, either. It seems like Nolan and Papsidera were intentionally trying to play against type and find someone who could channel an unseen part of themselves.

item.title: Data compiled by analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 has already raked in more than $750 million in preorders across both PlayStation 5 and Xbox.
item.description:
Data compiled by analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 has already raked in more than $750 million in preorders across both PlayStation 5 and Xbox.
GTA 6 launches in just two short weeks. It’s one of the most highly anticipated video game releases of all time and possibly the biggest pop culture phenomenon of this decade.
The hype for this particular entry is off the charts, and fans of Rockstar’s open-world action-adventure franchise are putting their money where their mouths are. According to data aggregated by Sensor Tower, Rockstar has already made three-quarters of the way to a billion dollars in preorders alone.
In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023
As of November 3, an estimated 7.71 million units have been sold, translating to a whopping $751 million in profits. The split between consoles is also notable; the amount of preorders on PlayStation is significantly higher than those on Xbox, with a 74% - 26% split.
This means that, on PlayStation, roughly $559 million in revenue was accrued; on Xbox, $192 million was made. Rockstar is making out like bandits, and the game hasn’t even come out yet.
For reference, GTA 5 made $800 million in its first 24 hours, and reached $1 billion in three days, making it the fastest entertainment product to reach $1 billion in history. It's possible that GTA 6 blows past this record, given what we're already seeing, but only time will tell once November 19 actually gets here.
These numbers are huge, and it’s likely due to fans purchasing the $100 Ultimate Edition of the game rather than its standard version. Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two Interactive, said as much in an August interview with CNBC, where he theorized this trend was “a reflection of the fact that the most avid consumers are the ones who are preordering now."
The Standard Edition of GTA 6 isn’t a whole lot cheaper. At $80, the base game also costs players a pretty penny — something that Zelnick told IGN was a reflection of the game’s value and actually a “bargain.”
“We aim always to deliver vastly more value than what we charge,” he said. “And we think that price point allows us to do just that. And then of course we have a premium opportunity for people who want to avail themselves of that. And even that one, again, we think is priced in a way so as to deliver much more value than what we're charging,” he told us.
“The truth is that the real cost of a AAA video game is a whole lot lower today than it was 20 years ago. Pricing has not kept pace with inflation. And our goal is to continue to over-deliver for our consumers, because how you feel about any experience is the intersection of the experience itself and what you pay for it. So to say that we expect that Grand Theft Auto 6 will be an incredible bargain as experiences go is a gross understatement, because Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.”
GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox X|S. For more interesting stats about the game, check out IGN’s report on how many players intend to take off work on release day, or see the concerning amount of fans who would give up their pets for a month for the chance to play it a week early.

item.title: Adam Driver says he's done with Star Wars and Kylo Ren, but would be open to a return if someone revived his cancelled solo film.
item.description:
Adam Driver says he's done with Star Wars and Kylo Ren, but would be open to a return if someone revived his canceled solo film.
Last year, Adam Driver and director Steven Soderbergh dropped a bombshell on Star Wars fans: They were working on a new film centered around Kylo Ren. It was meant to be a sequel to The Rise of Skywalker, which would have resurrected the somewhat redeemed sequel trilogy antagonist. However, Disney said no... because they couldn't buy into Kylo Ren coming back from the dead. The film was tentatively titled The Hunt for Ben Solo, and Star Wars leadership like Kathleen Kennedy also backed the project, but the bosses at Disney weren't as convinced.
Driver and Soderbergh developed the film for two years and seemed to be pretty passionate about it. However, Driver has given up hope of it ever happening, even in spite of fan campaigns. When speaking on The Rich Eisen Show, Driver was asked if he had a future in Star Wars. He stated that it was "over" and there would be "no more Star Wars" for him.
Key Moments in The Rise of Kylo Ren #3
Eisen asked if he would come back if The Hunt for Ben Solo were revived by Disney, and Driver said that he would, but he believes "the ship has sailed." This aligns with Lucasfilm boss Dave Filoni saying the movie was not in active development earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't hold out hope for this film ever getting made. Despite the fact that fans are consistently in a state of fury about the status of the Star Wars franchise and this movie was something they all rallied behind, Disney isn't interested.
It's also possible that Disney is trying to move on from the sequel trilogy, which got a progressively sour reputation with each installment. Disney is currently working on Star Wars Episode 10, with Spider-Man: No Way Home director Jon Watts in the driver's seat. It's unclear if the likes of Rey or Finn will reprise their roles in the project, or if Disney is going to create more distance between those films.
Steven Soderbergh has moved on from Star Wars and is now helping direct the final weeks of production on The Batman Part 2. The Oscar-winning filmmaker stepped in to help Matt Reeves, who had to depart the production during filming due to a personal matter. Soderbergh is working under the direction and vision of Reeves, with the intent to pass the baton back to him for post-production. Soderbergh himself has expressed disinterest in returning to The Hunt for Ben Solo, believing if it was going to happen, it would've already happened.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: A former member of Mob Entertainment’s Escape from Playtime Team claims “almost all” staff working on the project have been laid off.
item.description:
A former member of Mob Entertainment’s Escape from Playtime Team claims “almost all” staff working on the project have been laid off.
The news comes from a LinkedIn post penned by a former lead game designer at the studio on November 4, 2026.
“Today is a tough day,” they wrote. “Mob has laid off almost the entire Escape From Playtime team, including myself. If anyone knows of any work that I or any of the team affected can do, please reach out. This industry is tough, but the people band together to help each other out. Today that help is needed.
“For my friends affected at Mob I'm sorry, we did an amazing job, and pushed out a fantastic game. Be proud of what we accomplished. For those at Mob not affected, I will miss you all. Thank you for the opportunity to make EFP. Back to the grind.”
Poppy Playtime Figures from McFarlane Toys
Escape From Playtime is an online survival co-op game for two to eight players based on the horror mascot Poppy Playtime franchise. In the game, teams play as Smiling Critters plushes as they scavenge for resources and avoid monstrous mascot monsters. The spinoff was released on October 21, 2026; with so many staff being laid off just two weeks later, fans understandably grew worried about the game’s future.
Luckily, it has been confirmed that Escape From Playtime is still sticking around — at least, for now. On the game’s official Discord channel, Mob Entertainment's senior communications manager Tyler Sanchez spoke out about the layoffs and vaguely hinted at what’s next for the game. Sanchez said that development on the title will continue, outlining several improvements that are planned based on players’ feedback thus far.
“We've had to make the incredibly tough decision to part ways with some talented members of our team who helped bring Escape From Playtime to life. These are people who poured their creativity and passion into building this game and making it something special. We're incredibly grateful for everything they've contributed, and we want to take a moment to recognize the people behind the work. This isn't the kind of news we ever want to share, and we know it's difficult to hear, especially for a community that cares so deeply about the game and the people who make it,” he wrote.
“We also know that this will carry uncertainty from many of you about the future of Escape From Playtime. To be clear, development on the game continues. We've already made changes to the roadmap based on your feedback, including improvements to matchmaking, the order in which we'll roll out bigger body enemies, making the existing map more diverse and interesting, and much more.
“We know that news like this can bring a lot of questions, and it's important to us that we're transparent about where things stand. While we don't have every answer to share just yet, we'll continue to communicate the development process with you all.”

item.title: Maya Hawke has been cast in a ‘key’ role for Legendary’s live-action Magic: The Gathering movie, which is also planned to have a television series.
item.description:
Maya Hawke has been cast in a "key" role for Legendary’s live-action Magic: The Gathering movie, which is also planned to have a television series.
Magic: The Gathering’s live-action adaptation seems to have finally found its footing, with Deadline reporting that Stranger Things star Maya Hawke is the first actor to be officially cast in the film. Sources told the outlet that Hawke’s role is a "key" one, and that the project will have an "ensemble" feel. The same insiders said producers were focused on making sure she got the first offer to join.
It seems that Legendary and Hasbro have big plans in mind, as the iconic trading card game franchise is also set to receive a television universe. Canadian actor/director Matt Johnson is set to direct and write the film, alongside co-writers Aidan Fitzgerald and Noah Gardner.
Magic the Gathering: Star Trek – IGN Exclusive Card Reveals
Matt Johnson is best known for BlackBerry, a comedy-drama about the BlackBerry phone, and Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie, a sci-fi-ish comedy movie based on a web series he co-created. His filmography is a bit sparse, but given his comedy chops — along with Deadline’s report of an "ensemble cast" — it seems like the Magic: The Gathering movie could have a similar tone and feel to Dungeons and Dragons: Honor Among Thieves.
This is the latest news from this movie to surface after it was first confirmed in 2025 when Hasbro and Legendary announced their partnership and intentions to make an MTG movie. In July 2026, Vulture confirmed Matt Johnson’s involvement in the project, with storyboard artists, costume designers, and location scouts from Dune also reportedly lending their talents to the film.
Magic: The Gathering has faced decades of difficulty in its attempts to snag a screen adaptation. Its struggle first began in 2008, when Hasbro struck a deal with Universal to make movies based on several of its big brands, including MTG. Unfortunately, this project died a slow and painful death and, by 2012, it was ultimately canceled.
20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios) then snagged the film rights to Hasbro’s card game in 2014, which again sat in limbo until card designer Mark Rosewater confirmed the project was dead in 2022. This was especially painful, as several big names were attached to Fox’s MTG movie; Simon Kinberg (X-Men: Days of Future Past) was set to supervise, and Bryan Cogma — a writer for Game of Thrones — was also brought in to write the film.
Netflix also tried to snag a piece of the pie in the early 2020s with a live-action movie and an animated series that, unsurprisingly, also went nowhere. Now, Legendary and Hasbro are working hand-in-hand to finally bring MTG’s vibrant universe from cards to screens.
This is the latest big adaptation news to come from Legendary after the release of its Street Fighter movie this October, which proved to be a mixed bag among fans and critics but managed to secure top spot in the box office during its opening weekend.

item.title: K-pop girl group IVE is bringing its hit song "Love Dive" to the PUBG, complete with themed locations, character skins, choreography, and music videos.
item.description:
PUBG: Battlegrounds is no stranger to unusual collaborations, but its latest might be one of its most unexpected yet. K-pop girl group IVE is bringing its hit 2022 song "Love Dive" to the battle royale shooter, complete with themed locations, character skins, choreography, and music videos — further proof there is no scenario that cannot be improved with a bit of K-pop.
The collaboration is live now on PC and arrives on console November 12, bringing three special IVE locations across Rondo, all inspired by the "Love Dive" music video, including the IVE Mansion. We're also getting all six members represented with character likenesses, outfits, accessories, and weapon and gear skins. Across six maps, Rondo, Erangel, Miramar, Taego, Deston, and Vikendi, there are special IVE Emote Stages where you can perform one of the special IVE emotes to see a music video (on PC) or some album artwork on console. You can also look forward to Cupid's Crossbow and Cupid Chicken Man "interactive elements" on starting islands.
If you haven't yet discovered the total joy that is a good K-pop bop, the update also has something for players who prefer their PUBG experience with slightly less choreography and significantly more suffering. Two previous PvE modes are returning with increased difficulty.
HLB: Dawnbreakers of Rondo will get more frequent enemies, additional fuel requirements, and weaker defensive objectives and runs from November 4 to 25 on PC and November 12 to December 3 on consoles.
Returning roguelite mode Xeno Point: Hell trades the three OG difficulty levels for a single Hell difficulty and adds a tougher fourth sector. That mode runs from November 18 to December 2 on PC and November 26 to December 10 on console.
Whether you're dropping into Rondo for the chicken dinners or the choreography, PUBG's latest update certainly offers something a little different. I'm starting a petition for a Stray Kids collaboration immediately.

item.title: Cynthia Erivo, who you probably know best as Elphaba from the movie adaptation of Wicked, will play Afeni Shakur in the upcoming Snoop Dogg bopic Snoop.
item.description:
Cynthia Erivo, who you probably know best as Elphaba from the movie adaptation of Wicked, will play Afeni Shakur in the upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic Snoop. The movie started filming in September 2026, with Jonathan Daviss playing a young Snoop Dogg.
Tupac Shakur and Snoop Dogg reportedly first met on the set of the 1993 movie Poetic Justice and collaborated on tracks for Tupac's All Eyez on Me album.
Last month, Erivo explained how she chose her roles as an actress. "I feel like I have an internal metronome that tells me when something is right for me and when something is not," she told Hollywood Reporter. "I say no to a lot of things."
As well as being Tupac's mother, Afeni Shakur was a member of the Black Panther Party and an activist. After her son's death in 1996, she created the Georgia-based Tupac Amaru Shakur Foundation for young people interested in the arts and founded record label Amaru Entertainment to pulish her son's previously unreleased music.
The movie is scheduled for release on August 6, 2027.

item.title: Nathan Johnson was just elected as the new attorney general of Texas — but before he was in politics, he actually composed the music for 67 episodes of Dragon Ball Z.
item.description:
Nathan Johnson was just elected as the new attorney general of Texas — but before he was in politics, he actually composed the music for 67 episodes of Dragon Ball Z.
The United States midterm elections took place yesterday, November 3. The country’s Democratic party saw several major victories in this election, with the state of Texas being one of the most notable; for the first time in 30 years, the state ‘turned blue,’ with Democratic candidates James Talarico elected as U.S. senator and Gina Hinojosa as governor.
Another Democratic candidate who won the vote was Nathan Johnson, who was elected as Texas’ attorney general. Besides being the state’s first Democratic AG since 1994, he’s making headlines for a different, rather unexpected reason: He once composed the soundtrack for English episodes of Dragon Ball Z.
LEGO Dragon Ball Shenron & Goku
Johnson opened up about his past with the franchise in a June 22 Facebook post, where he described what it was like working on the famous anime series while being a father to young children.
“If you grew up watching Dragon Ball Z, you might know me better than you think: I composed the musical scores for 67 episodes and five movies, and had a great time doing it. Catching up recently with Taylor Rehmet, we talked about how composing for DBZ influenced my direction, and how the show still connects with so many Texans today,” he captioned the post.
“I had a one-year-old at the time, and I remember him sitting on my knee and stuff blowing up [on screen], and he’s like, ‘Oh, daddy, Goku!’ He just thought it was super cool. Even then, it got me street cred with my kids’ friends, and it gave me a creative outlet and a cultural connection that very few people have had the opportunity to have,” he said in his conversation with Rehmet.
Nathan Johnson was fascinated with music as a child, but decided to pursue a law degree in university, which has since come in handy in this recent election. However, before he became attorney general, he put his legal career on hold to pursue music, eventually crossing paths with one of Funimation’s co-founders, Robert Cocanaugher.
Cocanaugher was the landlord of a house he was hoping to rent. In a beautiful coincidence, this led to him being hired on as the second composer for Funimation’s in-house English dub of Dragon Ball Z. He was the last replacement composer used for the company’s dub, or any other English version of the anime, due to the Funimation’s music branch getting axed to cut costs.
Johnson spoke about his time at Funimation in an August 2012 interview with The Dao of Dragon Ball, saying he was nearly ready to quit his struggling music career when he first met Cocanaugher.
“A place near my house was for rent. I called the number on the sign out front to rent an office, and the guy on the phone said, ‘What will you use it for?’ I said ‘To practice law, but to be honest, I might throw an electric keyboard in there and make some musical noise, but nothing to disturb the other tenants.’ He said, ‘What kind of music?’ Well, it turned out the person on the phone and the owner of the building was Robert Cocanaugher," he said.
“I had never seen Dragon Ball, never heard of Dragon Ball Z in my life. Never seen an episode of an anime in my life. I had never scored anything commercial in my life. But Barry and obert apparently liked my music,” he continued. “...It was one of the most bizarre collisions of circumstance I’ve ever experienced.”
Johnson isn’t the only political candidate going viral for their connections to the entertainment space. Republican Marty O'Donnell, who composed music for the original Halo games and Destiny at Bungie, was the subject of a joke by winning Democratic opponent Susie Lee, who poked fun at his loss by posting the famous Vine of college students singing Halo’s monk chant in a bathroom.

item.title: Channing Tatum has debuted a slightly updated accent for Gambit in a new Avengers: Doomsday x Dunkin Donuts ad.
item.description:
Channing Tatum has debuted a slightly updated accent for Gambit in a new Avengers: Doomsday x Dunkin Donuts ad.
Tatum's Gambit made his debut in Deadpool and Wolverine with a very ridiculous, over-the-top Cajun accent. It worked for that film, given its inherent silliness, but it may be a bit jarring in a movie like Avengers: Doomsday, which seems to have a more serious tone compared to a Deadpool adventure. As a result, it seems like Tatum has toned it down a bit, but without making it feel dramatically different.
In a new Dunkin Donuts ad, Tatum's Gambit speaks with Herbie from the Fantastic Four film, allowing fans to hear a slightly more serious take on his character's voice. You can see a side-by-side comparison of his two appearances below.
Gambit’s accent in ‘Deadpool & Wolverine’ vs ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ https://t.co/3QQwAR7aUO
Last year, Tatum had teased that he wasn't going to go "full Cajun" with Gambit in Doomsday. He noted that it was important for the character to be able to be taken seriously, rather than feeling like some kind of parody.
“I’m not gonna go full Cajun," he said. "[The directors] want things to be funny, but they don’t want to go full Deadpool. They want to keep the drama and keep it tight. When Gambit gets serious — when he drops the Mardi Gras mask — things do matter.”
As of right now, it's unclear how big of a role Gambit will have in Avengers: Doomsday. He was a glorified cameo in Deadpool and Wolverine, but fans loved him, so it made sense to bring him back in a new film. Channing Tatum had originally been cast as Gambit in the 2010s for a solo film based on the character, but it unfortunately never went anywhere. Seeing that as an opportunity, Ryan Reynolds and the team behind Deadpool and Wolverine invited him to have a chance to finally play the character on the big screen.
It seems unlikely that Tatum's Gambit will be a primary player in the new X-Men film, which has a cast of mostly 20-somethings. Inde Navarette is set to play Rogue in the new film, and at 25 years old, it may not make sense to pair her with a 46-year-old version of Gambit. But hey, anything is possible!

item.title: Liam Neeson was apparently unaware that Meryl Streep is voicing Aslan in Greta Gerwig’s adaptation of The Magician’s Nephew — and his reaction to the news was priceless.
item.description:
Liam Neeson was apparently unaware that Meryl Streep is voicing Aslan in Greta Gerwig’s adaptation of The Magician’s Nephew — and his reaction to the news was priceless.
Greta Gerwig, who famously directed the Barbie movie, is turning C.S. Lewis’ vibrant fantasy world into a rock opera-style production. This unexpected and wildly different take on the source material has left audiences split; some are welcoming Gerwig’s quirky approach to the Narnia prequel with open arms, while others are left scratching their heads. ("Who asked for this?" is a common sentiment among those who are less excited about the film.)
Of the many notable choices Gerwig has made in her adaptation was the eyebrow-raising decision to cast Meryl Streep as the voice of the lion Aslan, a Christ-like figure in the books who sacrifices himself and is later reincarnated. In the original movie trilogy, Aslan was brought to life by Liam Neeson, who, up until recently, was totally unaware of who was inheriting the role in Gerwig’s movie — or, indeed, that another movie was being made, at all.
Neeson was informed about the film, as well as Streep’s casting, in a November 3 interview with ScreenRant, where he appeared completely blindsided by the news.
“I’m sorry — this is news to me,” Neeson said, visibly surprised.
“Well, I’m grateful to be the one to break it to you,” ScreenRant’s interviewer said.
“Oh. Great,” Neeson replied in a tone that can only be described as forced enthusiasm.
“Meryl Streep is taking on Aslan this time around,” the interviewer added.
“Meryl is playing Jesus Christ?” Neeson asked in clear disbelief. “Well, if you’re gonna make Christ a lady, nobody better than Meryl.” He then gave a winning smile.
Watch Liam Neeson learn about Meryl Streep voicing Aslan in Greta Gerwig's new Narnia adaptation in real time! 🦁 https://t.co/fgPmvtyPE8
Neeson’s remarks have, perhaps unsurprisingly, gone viral, and it seems that audiences have varying opinions as to what he said and what he actually meant. Some took his response to mean that he was feigning excitement about the project, while others congratulated him for his diplomatic response to the news, regardless of his true feelings on it.
“Poor guy got blindsided and reacted as diplomatically as possible. Class act,” one viewer on Twitter/X wrote.
“He’s so awesome for this response,” another said, while another remarked that his grin was the “worst fake smile I’ve ever seen.”
Still others pointed to a famous scene from Modern Family where Cameron Tucker says, “Excuse me. Meryl Streep could play Batman and be the right choice. She's perfection. Whether she's divorcing Kramer, whether she's wearing Prada... don't even get me started on Sophie's Choice. I get emotional thinking about it.” And to be honest, I’ve got to agree with both Tucker and Neeson here — if you’re going to have a woman play C.S. Lewis’ furry Christ allegory, then who better to cast than Meryl Streep?
Greta Gerwig’s The Magician’s Nephew comes to theaters on February 12, 2027.

item.title: Longtime Final Fantasy producer Yoshinori Kitase revealed to IGN that Star Wars was a big influence on the RPG franchise.
item.description:
Longtime Final Fantasy producer Yoshinori Kitase revealed to IGN that Star Wars was a big influence on the RPG franchise.
When speaking with IGN's Michael Peyton at the Lucca Comics & Games Festival 2026, Kitase was asked how he felt about Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 being heavily influenced by Final Fantasy. He admitted that he was really happy to see a game that was inspired by Square's RPG franchise have so much success, and that he himself is heavily inspired by other entertainment behemoths, too — namely Star Wars.
"To be honest, I know the game," Kitase said of Expedition 33. "I spoke with the creators and I'm actually very happy about the fact that they have been so inspired by Final Fantasy and they created a new game from that. And also, I was inspired by movies and in particular by Star Wars when I was young.
"I took inspiration from many things I was interested in when I was younger, and I used that inspiration to create my games. I think it's beautiful that there's this kind of cycle where we inspire each other and we take things from each other's games. I think it's something beautiful, and it should be like that."
The producer noted that he has always been careful not to lift directly from Star Wars, fearing that it would be too obvious and resemble more of a copy than anything else. However, he did point to a few things in his own work that were born from his love of the sci-fi series. He noted that Final Fantasy 7 characters Wedge and Biggs are the most overt inspirations, since they are named after characters from Star Wars' rebellion.
On a slightly more subtle note, he also noted that Blitzball from Final Fantasy 10 was inspired by Podracing from Star Wars: The Phantom Menace.
"One more that came to my mind is from Final Fantasy X, where I had to create [Blitzball] for the game inside the fantasy setting. And I used an idea from Star Wars Episode 1 where there's this [pod] race and the fact of using sport inside a fantasy context, I took this idea directly from Star Wars."
The highly-awaited conclusion to the Final Fantasy 7 remake trilogy, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, is set to release on April 8, 2027.

item.title: Yoshinori Kitase, producer of the Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy and director of the original Final Fantasy VII, was optimistic about the possibility of more movie adaptations for Final Fantasy games and hinted that Square Enix is likely interested in pursuing original IP moving forward.
item.description:
Yoshinori Kitase, producer of the Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy and director of the original Final Fantasy VII, was optimistic about the possibility of more movie adaptations for Final Fantasy games and hinted that Square Enix is likely interested in pursuing original IP moving forward.
It seems like every major video game developer is hawking out their IP for TV and film adaptations these days. And, for the most part, many of these have been quite successful: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie has become one of the most profitable horror films of all time, and the Sonic film franchise is so popular that a fourth movie is on the way.
One developer that’s been notably absent from this trend is Square Enix. While the Final Fantasy games have had their fair share of adaptations over the years to mixed reception from fans (The Spirits Within is a good movie, dammit, and I’ll die on this hill), we haven’t seen one on the big screen in quite some time.
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Preview Screenshots
IGN’s Michael Peyton got the chance to speak with Yoshinori Kitase at the Lucca Comics & Games Festival 2026, where he asked about Square Enix’s plans for future movies. And while Kitase couldn’t tell us much, his response was optimistic.
“Given the fact that we created this game, the remake of Final Fantasy VII, which explored the world of Final Fantasy VII way more than the original version, I think that it would be nice to have in the future games or TV series inspired by the story of Final Fantasy. And I don't see why that should not be a possibility in the future,” he answered.
What’s more, Kitase also seemed to be under the impression that Square Enix is likely to pivot its focus toward more original stories and IP, following the massive effort that is the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy.
“I think that mainly, we are more likely to invest in new titles and new games, but at the same time, for example, this time with the [Final Fantasy VII] remake, there was me and other creators who worked on the original game, which we had really strong feelings towards,” he said. “And we really wanted to create something new related to the old game to allow new users to play and to know the appeal of this game as much as the old users who play the old game. So there might be different cases like this one where the company is willing to invest in remaking old projects and other kinds of games like it happened this time.”
The third and final game in the Remake trilogy, Final Fantasy VII Revelation, releases on April 28, 2027 on PlayStation 5, Xbox X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC. For more information about the game, check out our hands-on preview from October, where we got the chance to play a section early and get a better feel for what the next chapter of Cloud’s journey will be like. You can read our full interview with Yoshinori Kitase here.

item.title: God of War Laufey will no longer be released in February, as Sony Santa Monica has pushed it back to May 2027.
item.description:
God of War Laufey will no longer be released in February, as Sony Santa Monica has pushed it back to May 2027.
The game will now launch on May 20, 2027, with the studio stating that it needs more time to make a product that meets fans' expectations. Sony Santa Monica also confirmed it would share more details on the game soon. It's possible we'll see something at The Game Awards, but there could also be a new State of Play before the end of the year (or very early 2027) that may reveal more about the next God of War installment.
An update regarding God of War Laufey's release date. https://t.co/qCw9O3dqtR
God of War Laufey had previously been slated to release on February 16, 2027. This window has become exceptionally crowded, especially after some games like Fable pivoted from a fall 2026 release to early 2027 to avoid the blast zone of GTA 6. This will not only give God of War some space to breathe, but potentially allow other games to stretch their wings that may not be as high on the priority list for gamers compared to a new first-party PlayStation game.
God of War Laufey has been met with no shortage of skepticism and criticism from some gamers, partially due to the fact that Kratos has been sidelined as the main character. As a result, it will be important for Santa Monica Studio to be on their A-game and deliver something exceptional. If there's anything that falls short of expectations, the internet will ruthlessly pick it apart, regardless of it's actually fair to do so.
The decision to delay the game must have been made relatively recently, as the studio had just announced a collector's box that was designed to coincide with the game's release date in February. It's unclear if that collector's box will be delayed as well, as it doesn't include the game and therefore is just a box of merch.
God of War Laufey will be one of the biggest games of 2027, as it will continue the story Sony Santa Monica set in motion back in 2018. Although Laufey is the protagonist, it is expected to overlap and connect back to the last two games, with Kratos also having a role in the new one. It's unclear what kind of larger implications and ramifications God of War Laufey will have on this universe, but it seems like a pretty significant expansion of the franchise. A new Kratos-led God of War title is also actively in the works.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Sonic is a cameo character in The Angry Birds Movie 3. The latest trailer shows him running, which is kinda his thing, alongside Chuck.
item.description:
Sonic is a cameo character in The Angry Birds Movie 3. The latest trailer shows him running, which is kinda his thing, alongside Chuck.
Chuck’s a yellow angry bird (he looks quite happy here, to be fair), voiced by Josh Gad, who you probably know best as Frozen’s Olaf. The pair run through a forest in the trailer, laughing and smiling about some mysterious shenanigans.
In the games, Sonic is always looking to save the woodland creatures, so I suppose it’s not a huge leap for him to be around the Angry Birds. Maybe he’ll teach them how to spin up so they can launch themselves at pig structures in devastating new ways. That’ll show the pigs.
This is the first Angry Birds flick under Paramount. The previous two movies were headed up by Sony, but now Paramount's at the helm and Paramount owns the movie rights to Sonic, working in partnership with Sega. Jason Sudeikis returns as Red for The Angry Birds Movie 3, while John Rice steps into the director’s chair. Rice previously co-directed the second movie and was lead storyboard artist on the first film.
Here's the trailer:
“We are thrilled to announce that the brand-new film of the globally beloved and successful Angry Birds franchise is to be in production,” said Shuji Utsumi, President and COO at Sega, when Angry Birds 3 was initially announced. “Sega has been focusing on its Transmedia strategy to advance the value of its intellectual properties across games and diverse media landscapes.
“We believe that the upcoming The Angry Birds Movie 3 perfectly aligns with our strategy and presents a great opportunity for us to bring the charm of the Angry Birds brand to fans across the globe.”
Angry Birds 3 is coming to theaters on December 23. If you don’t want to see Sonic reduced to a cameo, you could always wait for Sonic the Hedgehog 4, which is coming to movie theatres on March 19.

item.title: Dr. Doom is teaming up with a particularly powerful ally: Colonel Sanders.
item.description:
Dr. Doom is teaming up with a particularly powerful ally: Colonel Sanders.
KFC announced its official Avengers: Doomsday campaign with a commercial showing Dr. Doom looking out on the Fallout-esque ruins of New York. Doomsday has arrived, it seems, and while even the Avengers Tower has fallen to the wreckage, one KFC location stands strong.
"KFC has come to an agreement with Dr. Doom," says the overlay. "All it took was a meal worthy of his name."
Fans will get the chance to try this meal for themselves when the official Dr. Doom menu launches across select KFC locations on November 9.
First promo for the KFC and ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ collab. https://t.co/JAwNxGAuAa
Every "Doomified" purchase comes in limited-edition packaging inspired by Dr. Doom's green and black look, and also comes with one of five Colonel Sanders Cosplay Collection figurines, while supplies last.
The Doom-approved menu is powered by three new flavors: a Smoky Green Mayo, a sweet and caramelized Doom Cola sauce, and a smoky charred lime and chili seasoning KFC is calling Doom Dust. The Dr. Doom Menu adds various combinations of these new flavors to existing KFC classics, like Dripped Wings, Loaded Fries, and the classic Chicken Bucket.
The Doomsday takeover isn't just about flavor, however, as the image below shows KFC going all-in on the Marvel villain’s color theme. The Doom Burger features the Smoky Green Mayo leaking like ectoplasm off of the patty. A black sesame bun brings the burger to sci-fi territory.
While the Doom Cola sauce is central to the new menu items, KFC is actually going an entirely different direction with its Doomified drinks. The vanilla-flavored Doom Shake is filled with chocolate and peppermint sauce (you can also choose a green apple sauce) to achieve a jarring green and black appearance. A Doom Supreme Fizz combines sparkling lemonade, green apple syrup (or kiwi), and boba pearls.
The Doom Menu also lists Masked Mozza Melts, a batch of mozzarella sticks served with the new Dr. Doom sauces, which puts the collaboration in direct competition with another Marvel campaign, Jack in the Box's Doomsday Dipper Box.
As for the collectable side of things, the image above only shows one of the Doomified Colonel Sanders figures, who's donned the cloaked look of his villainous new ally to enjoy a big bucket of fried chicken.
Avengers: Doomsday Trailer: First Look at Doctor Doom
Dr. Doom, which sees Iron Man alum Robert Downey Jr. returning to the MCU, has unsurprisingly become the central character in Marvel’s marketing for Avengers: Doomsday. The KFC collaboration lands ahead of the movie’s release in theaters on December 18, and will be available through the new year.
"This is KFC's most expansive joint venture to date,” said Scott Mezvinsky, global CEO of KFC. “This isn't just about chicken – it's about putting KFC at the heart of a global cultural phenomenon in the most epic way we could."

item.title: Nvidia just showed off DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy in a new video that shows how its AI-enhanced lighting and materials model looks in-game. It’s a much more subtle effect compared to the images and clips going around after a leaked early version of DLSS 5 was modded into games.
item.description:
Nvidia just showed off DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy in a new video that shows how its AI-enhanced lighting and materials model looks in-game. It’s a much more subtle effect compared to the images and clips going around after a leaked early version of DLSS 5 was modded into games.
Before, it looked like those yassification filters that were popular for like a week. It smoothed characters over, weirdly made some look about 30 years older, and generally warped the intended art style into something uncanny.
“On Thursday, November 5th, in collaboration with Warner Bros. Games and Avalanche Software, Hogwarts Legacy is updating the game to integrate DLSS 5 technology to enhance the lighting and materials, and use DLSS 5’s model controls to boost environmental uplift while preserving character identity,” Nvidia said.
According to the gargantuan tech company, DLSS 5 isn’t just a switch to be flipped — developers have to fine tune it and approve before release to hit the desired effect. It isn’t just about characters’ faces either. With the Neural Rendering option enabled, Nvidia claims shadows pop more, textures are upscaled, and reflections are sharper as the tech works in real-time to paint over the scene. You can see how it looks in Hogwarts Legacy in the video below.
Here's the official blurb from Nvidia:
DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering will be available starting November 5th in Hogwarts Legacy for all GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and laptops, RTX Spark PCs, and GeForce NOW Ultimate. With the Neural Rendering option enabled, detail and shadows in environments are enhanced, texture detail on characters is improved, shading and lighting is refined, and reflections are more vibrant.
With the addition of DLSS with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to Hogwarts Legacy, our complete suite of DLSS technologies is now supported, enabling you to accelerate and enhance your experiences in the wizarding world.
For an optimal experience, we also recommend enabling DLSS Super Resolution under “Upscale Type,” DLSS Multi Frame Generation under “Frame Generation,” NVIDIA Reflex under “Low Latency Mode,” and “DLSS Ray Reconstruction” if you’re also activating Hogwarts Legacy’s immersive ray-traced effects.
With DLSS 5 activated, Ray Reconstruction, 6X Multi Frame Generation, NVIDIA Reflex, and ray tracing enabled, the game runs at up to 300 FPS at 4K on the GeForce RTX 5090.
